source.section: Dynamic Capacity Allocation for Elective Surgeries: Reducing
source.quote: The large state space and detailed system dynamics lead us to simulation-based dynamic programming approaches for ﬁnding good capacity allocation decisions.

The state space includes all possible combinations of patients waiting for each specialty and urgency level (as well as waiting time in the case of convex penalty costs), and the action space includes all possible ways to allocate capacity so as to satisfy constraints (2).

After the initial allocation corrections are made in period 1 (which we note must still be within the maximum 20% change allowed by the hospital), we measure the remaining variability in periodic allocations using the standard deviation of hours allocated to each service in periods 2–10 (the end of the horizon).
